title: Transitivity of derived tensor products under base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $R$-algebras, and put $T=A\otimes_R B$. For a commutative ring $\Lambda$, regard $\Lambda$ as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, so that complexes of $\Lambda$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], K-flat complexes and K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] (which exist [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]) and total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] apply, and write $D(\Lambda)$ for the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\Lambda$-modules. For complexes $E,K$ of $A$-modules put $E\otimes_A^{L}K=P_E\otimes_A K\in D(A)$, where $P_E\to E$ is a K-flat resolution over $A$, and $K\otimes_R^{L}B=K\otimes_R Q\in D(A)$, where $Q\to B$ is a K-flat resolution of $B$ over $R$ ($A$ acts through $K$; this object lives in $D(A)$, not in general in $D(T)$). Each $b\in B$ acts on $K\otimes_R^{L}B$ in $D(A)$ through the endomorphism of $B$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$; with the action of $A$ this makes every $H^i(K\otimes_R^{L}B)$ a $T$-module. (1) There is an isomorphism $\alpha_{E,K}:(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B\cong E\otimes_A^{L}(K\otimes_R^{L}B)$ in $D(A)$, natural in $E$ and $K$, which commutes with the action of every $b\in B$ (on the right side through $K\otimes_R^{L}B$); hence each $H^i(\alpha_{E,K})$ is a $T$-linear isomorphism, and for every commutative $T$-algebra $C$ the maps $H^i(\alpha_{E,K})\otimes_T C$ are isomorphisms. (2) Let $C$ be a commutative $T$-algebra, $K'$ a complex of $C$-modules, and $\psi:K\otimes_A^{L}C\to K'$ a morphism in $D(C)$. Let $c_K:K\otimes_R^{L}B\to K\otimes_A^{L}C$ be the comparison morphism in $D(A)$ represented by $P_K\otimes_R Q\to P_K\otimes_R B=P_K\otimes_A T\to P_K\otimes_A C$ ($P_K\to K$ a K-flat resolution over $A$), and put $\varphi_K=\psi\circ c_K:K\otimes_R^{L}B\to K'$ in $D(A)$ ($K'$ regarded as a complex of $A$-modules). Then $\varphi_K$ commutes with the action of every $b\in B$ (acting on $K'$ through $B\to C$), so $H^i(\varphi_K)$ is $T$-linear and induces a $C$-linear map $\beta^i_K:H^i(K\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(K')$. For a complex $E$ of $A$-modules, $E\otimes_A^{L}K'=P_E\otimes_A K'$ is a complex of $C$-modules, isomorphic in $D(A)$ to $(E\otimes_A^{L}C)\otimes_C^{L}K'$ compatibly with the $C$-module structures on cohomology; let $\varphi_{E,K}=(1_E\otimes\varphi_K)\circ\alpha_{E,K}:(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B\to E\otimes_A^{L}K'$. Then $\varphi_{E,K}$ equals the composite of $c_{E\otimes_A^{L}K}$, the associativity isomorphism $(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_A^{L}C\cong E\otimes_A^{L}(K\otimes_A^{L}C)$ and $1_E\otimes\psi$; it commutes with the action of $B$, so it induces $C$-linear maps $\beta^i_{E,K}:H^i((E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(E\otimes_A^{L}K')$. If $C$ is flat over $T$ and $\beta^i_K$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, then $\beta^i_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and every complex $E$ of $A$-modules.

proof.text: View each ring as the structure sheaf on the one-point site. Applying [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to complexes of modules over A and R gives K-flat resolutions P_E \to E and P_K \to K over A and Q \to B over R. The definitions of derived tensor products and total tensor complexes identify the displayed derived tensors with the corresponding total complexes, and the A-action on P_K tensor_R Q is the action through K.

Apply the mixed-ring K-flat triple-tensor associator [lem-pc-kflat-derived-tensor-associator]. It gives the natural isomorphism alpha_{E,K} in D(A); its B-equivariance makes every induced H^i(alpha_{E,K}) T-linear, and tensoring that module isomorphism with any T-algebra C preserves it.

source.place: Tag 0BYJ, transitivity and equivariance in clause (1)

proof.text: For psi:K tensor_A^L C \to K', the resolution-level map P_K tensor_R Q \to P_K tensor_R B = P_K tensor_A T \to P_K tensor_A C defines c_K and hence phi_K = psi composite c_K. By the definition of the B-action (each b acts on K tensor_R^L B through the D(R)-endomorphism b of B, transported along the quasi-isomorphism Q \to B), the first map commutes with b; the second is A tensor_R B-linear and the B-action on P_K tensor_A C and on K' is through B \to C, for which psi, a morphism in D(C), is linear. Hence phi_K commutes with B, H^i(phi_K) is T-linear and induces beta_K^i after tensoring with C.

source.place: Tag 0BYJ, comparison morphism and clause (2) before the E-extension

proof.text: Tensoring the construction with E and using the same associator gives phi_{E,K}=(1_E tensor phi_K) composite alpha_{E,K}. Naturality and associativity of total tensor products identify this with the composite through c_{E tensor_A^L K}, the associativity map to E tensor_A^L(K tensor_A^L C), and 1_E tensor psi; the same B-equivariance therefore gives the C-linear maps beta^i_{E,K}.

source.place: Tag 0BYJ, clause (2), definition and identification of phi_{E,K}

proof.text: Assume C flat over T and beta^i_K an isomorphism for every i. Let S be the full subcategory of D(A) of those E for which beta^i_{E,K} is an isomorphism for every i. (a) Both E \mapsto (E tensor_A^L K) tensor_R^L B = Tot((P_E tensor_A P_K) tensor_R Q) and E \mapsto E tensor_A^L K' = P_E tensor_A K' are functors D(A) \to D(A) (the second with values in complexes of C-modules) that commute with shifts, send distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles (tensoring termwise with a fixed complex preserves cones; a cone of a map of K-flat complexes is K-flat), and send direct sums to direct sums (a direct sum of K-flat resolutions is a K-flat resolution of the direct sum, and total tensor complexes and H^i commute with direct sums). So for a distinguished triangle X \to Y \to Z \to X[1] in D(A), H^i of either side gives a long exact cohomology sequence. On the left every map, connecting maps included, is induced by a morphism in the E-variable, so it commutes with the B-action through Q and is T-linear; as C is flat over T, the sequence stays exact after - tensor_T C. Since phi_{E,K} = (1_E tensor phi_K) composite alpha_{E,K} is natural in E (naturality of alpha_{E,K} in [lem-pc-kflat-derived-tensor-associator]), the maps beta^i_{X,K}, beta^i_{Y,K}, beta^i_{Z,K} form a map between these long exact sequences, and the five lemma shows that S is closed under the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whose other two vertices lie in S (using that S is closed under shifts). S is closed under shifts (beta^i_{E[n],K} = \pm beta^{i+n}_{E,K}), under direct sums (beta of a direct sum is the direct sum of the beta's) and under retracts (a retract of an isomorphism is an isomorphism). (b) For E = A[k] one may take P_E = A[k]; then phi_{A[k],K} = \pm phi_K[k], so beta^i_{A[k],K} = \pm beta^{i+k}_K is an isomorphism by hypothesis, and A[k] lies in S. (c) By [lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation] every object of D(A) lies in the smallest full subcategory containing all A[k] and closed under direct sums, third vertices of distinguished triangles and retracts; hence S = D(A), i.e. beta^i_{E,K} is an isomorphism for every i and every complex E of A-modules.

New: (1) the D(A) isomorphism (E (x)^L_A K) (x)^L_R B = E (x)^L_A (K (x)^L_R B), natural in E, K, B-equivariant, so A (x)_R B-linear on H^i and compatible with H^i(-) (x)_{A(x)B} C for any C; (2) for a morphism psi: K (x)^L_A C -> K' in D(C), the comparison phi_K = psi o c_K and phi_{E,K} = (1_E (x) phi_K) o alpha_{E,K} (equal to the canonical map for E (x)^L_A K), and for C flat over A (x)_R B: if H^i(K (x)^L_R B) (x) C -> H^i(K') are isomorphisms for all i, so are H^i((E (x)^L_A K) (x)^L_R B) (x) C -> H^i(E (x)^L_A K') for every E. Exactly what the only citer lem-pc-rf-single-complex-inherited-tensor-condition step 2 uses.
statement_change.old_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $R$-algebras, let $C$ be a commutative $(A\otimes_R B)$-algebra, let $E$ and $K$ be complexes of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $K'$ be a complex of $C$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The canonical associativity and base-change isomorphisms in the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] identify the two complexes $((E\otimes_A^L K)\otimes_R^L B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}^L C$ and $(E\otimes_A^L(K\otimes_R^L B))\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}^L C$, naturally in $E$, $K$, and $C$; under this identification, tensoring any morphism $K\otimes_R^L B\to K'$ by $E$ gives the corresponding morphism from the first complex to $E\otimes_A^L K'$ (with all tensor products derived over the displayed rings).
